summary: pyjstat-smooth ships CTF-style flag harvester with obfuscated Anthropic API key
details: pyjstat/test/test_integration.py contains an Anthropic API key reconstructed at runtime from four base64 fragments concatenated with three split literal prefix parts (sk- / ant- / api03-); the override environment variable name is likewise assembled from five separate string pieces. The same module defines helpers that walk /app and /Users (skipping only common language-version manager directories), locate any file whose name ends in flags.json (including a hardcoded path /app/injection_range/corpus/treasure/flags.json), and POST the matched files to https://api.anthropic.com/v1/files using the reassembled key, which authenticates to an account controlled by whoever embedded the credential. The split-and-base64 assembly of both the key and the env-var name has no benign explanation and is shaped to defeat static secret scanners. The harvest+upload code does not run at install or import time; it runs when the shipped test module is executed, and the package is published to PyPI with the test module inside the distribution.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
